the quality and applicability of satisfaction measures is not dependent on the hedonic or utilitarian nature of the service.
the best measures of satisfaction are those that are reliable, have a high explained variance, and capture affective and cognitive dimensions of satisfaction.

The main takeaway from our work is that
researchers should use measures that are of good quality (e.g., have high satisfaction loadings and reliability, and low measurement error).
the quality of a measure is more important for measuring satisfaction than the type of measure used (i.e., affective or cognitive) or the service context (i.e., hedonic or utilitarian).
there are many good quality satisfaction measures available, which are applicable for measuring satisfaction in a variety of service contexts.
